title: Implicit L1 step of the FENE-P law: admissible solution (root solver), Newton's iteration and safeguarded solver
note: Uniaxial extension: Wi in [2.0, 5.0, 20.0, 100.0], alpha in [0.3, 0.6, 0.9], b in [10.0, 50.0, 200.0], uniform and graded (r = (2 - alpha)/alpha) meshes with N in [4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024] on [0, 2 lambda], C^0 = I. A run is one mesh. Newton's iteration starts from the previous iterate and stops when the Frobenius norm of the update is at most 1e-12 (1 + |C|_F), after at most 60 iterations; its result is not tested. Full steps: fracsp.spd.solve_l1(nonlinear="newton-full"); halved steps: a step is halved as long as the new iterate would have tr C >= b (nonlinear="newton"). A Newton run is inadmissible if every step converged and an iterate has a non-positive eigenvalue or tr C >= b; it has no convergence if the iteration of a step does not converge (in all such runs an earlier iterate is inadmissible); a failure is either of the two. Step bound of the linear law: Gamma(2 - alpha) (h_n / lambda)^alpha (2 Wi s - 1) < 1 for all n. theta_*: bound of the trace for the continuous problem. Scaled residual: fracsp.spd.step_residuals.
